meta.title: Token Pacer: never hit the cap by surprise
meta.description: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and more: your quotas live in your Mac's notch. Real numbers, straight from each provider. No account, no API key, no permissions.
meta.ogAlt: Token Pacer: a green-to-red usage scale at 62%, with 2h 14m to reset.

hero.eyebrow: For macOS · lives in the notch
headlines: Never hit the cap by surprise
hero.sub: You find out you were at 94% by being told you're at 100%, mid-task, on the afternoon it matters. Token Pacer keeps Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and more in front of you all day, so you never have to ask.

features.label: Always there, never in the way
features.note: Lives in the notch. No notch? It docks in the menu bar, on whichever display you pick.

features.label: Every agent, side by side
features.note: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and more on one scale, each on its own reset. Click one to pin it to the menu bar.

features.label: Real numbers only
features.note: Every figure is the provider's own. When one can't be read, it says so and why. Never a guess.

features.label: Warns you once, then waits
features.note: Give each agent its own amber and red lines. Cross one and the pill opens by itself until you look.

features.label: Nothing to sign into
features.note: No account, no API key, no permission prompts. It reads the CLI you already run and sends nothing but an update check.

features.label: Light on the Mac it watches
features.note: Native Swift, no web view. The drawing runs on CoreAnimation, so it idles cheap and stays cool.

press.heading: Press kit
press.sub: Everything you need to write about Token Pacer. Use any of it, no need to ask.
press.short: Token Pacer puts your quotas for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and more in your Mac’s notch, so you never hit the cap by surprise.
press.long: You usually find out you were at 94% by being told you’re at 100%, mid-task. Token Pacer is a free macOS app that keeps Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and more in the notch all day, with each provider’s real numbers and reset times. No account, no API key, no permissions. It’s native Swift, idles cheap, warns you once when you cross the amber or red line you set, and docks in the menu bar on Macs without a notch.
